decisions.quote: However, the results from VD 2.0 are fundamentally different to those from VD 1.0 (Figure 5b). Severe cover loss is limited to small areas and the magnitude of cover change is smaller compared to VD 1.0. Overall, net cover change is positive with 18% of areas showing a decreasing trend of vegetation cover, while half (50%) of all semi-natural areas exhibit an increase (Table 4).
decisions.reason: This study is a replication of Hostert et al. (2003) [42] across an expanded island-wide Crete sample and 1984-2006 period using 2,816 Landsat images. The outcome is failed rather than mixed or statistically successful but flawed: under the codebook, statistically successful but flawed applies when the replication obtains the original effect (so it would otherwise be coded successful) but argues the method is invalid, whereas here the actual full-archive replication test (VD 2.0) did not obtain the original vegetation-decline finding at all and instead reversed the net trend to positive gain (50% increasing vs. 18% decreasing). The restricted 14-date VD 1.0 analysis was constructed solely as a comparison baseline because dropping pre-1984 MSS data and expanding the study area precluded direct numerical comparison with [42], and expert validation rejected 67.1% of VD 1.0 trends (confirming only 32.9% vs. 98.7% for VD 2.0) as spurious phenological timing artifacts explaining why the original finding failed to replicate.
